prerequisites: Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the methods of electromagnetic field theory.
They are aware that electromagnetic fields act on electrical circuits and could influence their behavior.
They are also aware that the influence of electromagnetic fields becomes critical particularly at high frequencies and with long lines.
Students can apply vector analysis to calculate scalar and vector fields.
They can use Maxwell's equations for the analytical calculation of simple electromagnetic field distributions.
They can perform the calculation and design of the components discussed.
They can apply the methods to simple electrical engineering systems.
Students furthermore know how electromagnetic fields affect current flow in conductors.
They understand how the laws of electrodynamics lead to the propagation of electromagnetic waves.
They independently work out solutions to practice problems.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical foundations of vector analysis, scalar and vector fields, gradient, divergence, curl, integral theorems (Gauss, Stokes)
Maxwell's equations, material equations, boundary and auxiliary conditions
Static fields: Electro- and magnetostatics, potential function and work integral, boundary conditions, potential equations, capacitance and energy in the electrostatic field
Stationary fields: Stationary current and magnetic fields, boundary conditions, magnetic vector potential, Biot-Savart law
Quasistationary fields: Induction law, inductance, energy conversions in the electromagnetic field, calculation of quasistationary electromagnetic fields, cylindrical current-carrying conductor
Electromagnetic wave fields: Continuity equation, wave equation, wave fields with harmonic time dependence
assessment_rules: The module grade is based on a graded oral examination, which accounts for 100% of the module's overall grade.
